findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and silently drops the queued DB deletes
findings.body: In the new cancellation block of the cron handler, the loop awaits `client.request` for each cancelled reminder and collects `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` promises into `workflowRemindersToDelete`, awaiting them only after the loop. If any single SendGrid request throws (e.g. batch_id already gone, rate limit, network error), the loop exits immediately: (1) all remaining cancelled reminders are not cancelled at SendGrid this run, and (2) the delete promises already collected are never awaited — Prisma promises are lazy, so those rows are never deleted. The rows already cancelled at SendGrid but not deleted will be re-cancelled on the next run (harmless but noisy), while rows not yet reached keep their scheduled emails alive. Each reminder's cancel+delete should be isolated in its own try/catch, and the DB delete should be awaited per reminder.

findings.title: Reschedule path uses immediate SendGrid cancel, re-creating the 100-pending-cancellation pile-up the PR intends to fix
findings.body: When a booking is rescheduled, the old booking's email reminders are cancelled via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` with `immediateDelete=true`, which immediately POSTs `status: "cancel"` to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends`. Per the PR description, every such POST creates a pending cancellation entry in SendGrid that persists until the scheduled send date (up to 72 hours away) and SendGrid caps pending cancellations at 100 — the exact root cause of the bug being fixed. The plain-cancel path (handleCancelBooking) was changed to only set `cancelled=true` and let the cron cancel within 1 hour of the send date, which bounds pending cancellations; the reschedule path bypasses that mechanism. It also leaves the old WorkflowReminder rows in the DB with `scheduled=true, cancelled=false` (the immediateDelete branch returns without deleting or flagging the row), so they linger until their scheduledDate passes. The reschedule path should use the same `cancelled=true` flag flow as booking cancellation.

findings.title: immediateDelete path in deleteScheduledEmailReminder never deletes or flags the WorkflowReminder row
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` (used here for workflow deletion and deleted steps, and in handleNewBooking for reschedules) cancels the send at SendGrid but then returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or setting `cancelled=true`. For workflow/step deletion the rows are removed by the onDelete: Cascade, but for the reschedule call site in handleNewBooking the rows survive with `scheduled=true, cancelled=false` until their scheduledDate passes and the cron's generic deleteMany removes them — meanwhile nothing in the system knows their SendGrid send is already cancelled. Either delete the row in the immediateDelete branch or set `cancelled=true` so state stays consistent.

findings.title: Cancellation query lacks method filter and only covers a 1-hour window, so a missed cron run can leak sends
findings.body: The `remindersToCancel` query filters only on `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1h` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` filter and no `referenceId` non-null check. It works today only because no other code path sets `cancelled=true` for SMS reminders; that implicit coupling is fragile. More importantly, the design relies on the cron running at least once every hour: if the cron is down or delayed beyond the 1-hour window after a reminder is flagged cancelled, the reminder's scheduledDate passes, the first `deleteMany` in the same handler removes the row without ever posting the SendGrid cancellation, and SendGrid delivers the email for a cancelled booking. Consider also cancelling already-due cancelled reminders before the deleteMany (or making the deleteMany exclude `cancelled: true` rows).
